(1) packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Balance.tsx:102-103 is still `id.slice(8).split('/')[0]`, and a grep for `slice(8)` across packages/ returns that one line and no other — it is the only remaining hand-rolled preview-id parse, and the five sibling call sites (Account.tsx:1562 plus the four mobile AccountTransactions files) already import parsePreviewId. (2) `ls upcoming-release-notes/` shows both post-scheduled-transaction-on-its-own-date.md and fix-schedule-occurrence-consumption.md, same category Bugfixes, same single author Shivam-Fl, for one shipped change. (3) `git show 97938bb -- packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts` shows the setNextDate hunk is a pure re-indentation plus the `nextDate` -> `currentNextDate` rename: the `if (dateCond) { ... }` body and the local name exist in HEAD~1 (9065a36) and the current signature ({id, conditions, reset, advance}) is unchanged, so no caller passes the removed explicit nextDate. validated_work_order.understanding: PR #15 (commit 97938bb) left three pieces of its own scaffolding behind, none of them worth its own ticket. First, the desktop account register's SelectedBalance still parses a preview row id by hand at Balance.tsx:102-103 (`id.slice(8).split('/')[0]`) while every other caller — the desktop register's onScheduleAction in Account.tsx:1562 and the four mobile *AccountTransactions.tsx handlers — reads the schedule id through `parsePreviewId` from `@actual-app/core/shared/transactions`. `id.slice(8)` assumes the literal `preview/` sits at offset 0; parsePreviewId splits instead. For every id the producer actually makes (`preview/<scheduleId>/<YYYY-MM-DD>`, built at packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:607) the two forms return the same schedule id, so this is a consistency fix, not a behaviour fix, and the existing Balance.test.tsx preview cases pass either way. Second, upcoming-release-notes/ carries two Bugfixes notes crediting the same author for one user-facing change: post-scheduled-transaction-on-its-own-date.md is the leftover of the force-pushed-over revision and describes the advance-the-schedule mechanism that #15 deleted (advanceScheduleToDate is gone; postTransactionForSchedule now refuses to post an occurrence already stamped), while fix-schedule-occurrence-consumption.md describes the per-occurrence model that actually shipped. Third, the same commit flattened setNextDate's `if (dateCond) { ... }` into a `dateCond ? ... : null` ternary and renamed the local `nextDate` to `currentNextDate`, to accommodate an explicit nextDate parameter that a later commit in the same PR removed. Nothing about the function's behaviour changed — the two forms are semantically identical — so ~25 lines of the schedule write path now carry pure re-indentation and a name no reviewer would pick. Restoring main's shape is a mechanical revert of one hunk, pinned by the existing schedules tests. Nothing a user sees changes.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #15 was force-pushed over mid-review: the earlier revision advanced next_date through the posted occurrence via an `advanceScheduleToDate` helper and gave setNextDate an explicit nextDate parameter, and the surviving revision replaced both with per-occurrence consumption. The final squash kept the three edits the intermediate revisions needed — Balance.tsx's inline id parse, the second release note, and the setNextDate re-indentation and rename — none of which the shipped design needed.
validated_work_order.approach: Four mechanical edits, no new behaviour. (1) Balance.tsx: widen the existing `@actual-app/core/shared/transactions` import to `{ isPreviewId, parsePreviewId }` and replace the two inline lines with `const { scheduleId } = parsePreviewId(id);`, dropping the `preview/<schedule_id>/<date>` comment because that format is now documented on parsePreviewId itself (packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts:17-25). The `date` field of the returned object is deliberately unused: SelectedBalance sums schedule._amount, which is identical for every occurrence of one schedule, and each occurrence already has its own row in `selectedItems`, so the existing two-occurrence test still expects -100.00. (2) Delete upcoming-release-notes/post-scheduled-transaction-on-its-own-date.md and fold its one still-true clause — the transaction lands on the occurrence you clicked and that Upcoming row leaves the register — into the surviving note's single body line; frontmatter is untouched. (3) packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts: revert the setNextDate hunk to commit 9065a36's text exactly, so the body reads `// Only do this if a date condition exists` / `if (dateCond) { ... }` with the local named `nextDate`. The reference image is HEAD~1, not HEAD: `git show HEAD~1:packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts` — the ticket's `git show main:...` names the wrong commit in this fork because the branch already has #15 merged. (4) Change nothing else: no signature change, no new parameter, no test edits.

risks: setNextDate is date arithmetic in the schedule write path. The two forms are semantically identical (`dateCond ? ... : null` then `if (newNextDate != null ...)` is `if (dateCond) { const newNextDate = ...; if (...) }`), so the risk is a bad mechanical revert, not a design mistake — which is why the QA script diffs the whole function against `git show HEAD~1:` rather than asking anyone to read it. The five call sites (app.ts:439 reset:true, 446 reset:true, 467 advance:true via skipNextDate, 661 and 796 advance:true) are all inside this function's blast radius.

The release-notes gate cannot run in this fork, and would object to this diff if it did. packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs requires `added.length !== 0` over `--diff-filter=AMR` — a deletion-only diff reports 'No release note added'. The surviving note here is edited, not added. No workflow in .github/workflows invokes that script (only ci-verify.yml and the sdlc-*.yml files exist; the upstream release-notes.yml was not imported), and .github/** is a forbidden path, so wiring it up is out of scope. AC-2 is therefore written against the surviving note satisfying that script's own validateFile rules — category in categoryOrder, authors free of bots, exactly one non-empty body line — which it does. If a human later imports the upstream workflow, this PR would need a note renamed rather than deleted to satisfy the `added` requirement.

The commit named in the ticket, 37cc794, does not exist in this repository's history — the fork's first commit is 32324e6 ('Import actualbudget/actual at 3ef90fe'). The rename and re-indentation came from 97938bb instead, and its pre-image is 9065a36. An implementer who follows the ticket's `git show main:...` literally will diff the function against itself and conclude there is nothing to revert; the QA script's diff against HEAD~1 is the authoritative comparison.

Deleting the duplicate note drops a sentence the changelog would otherwise have carried ('posting a later upcoming occurrence ... the upcoming row it came from stayed in the register'). That clause is still true of the shipped code — postTransactionForSchedule uses `date ?? schedule.next_date` — so the survivor's body must gain it. If the implementer deletes the leftover without carrying the clause across, the release notes under-describe the shipped change and AC-2 fails.

Balance.tsx's `slice(8)` and parsePreviewId differ for one class of id: any string containing 'preview/' but not at offset 0 (isPreviewId uses indexOf, so it admits them). No such id is produced — the preview id is built at packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:607 — so neither behaviour is observable today; this is why the change is filed as consistency and no new test is written.

No path in forbidden_paths is touched: .sdlc/**, .github/**, packages/ci-actions/src/migrations/**, packages/loot-core/src/mocks/migrations/**, packages/loot-core/src/server/migrate/** and the sync-server migration paths are all outside the four files named above.
The change adds no host to env.api_allowlist and sends no data anywhere; it is pure local refactoring plus one markdown deletion.
